stem: In a school garden in Pune, students have a small pond with pondweed, tadpoles and small fish. One season, a gardener removes most of the pondweed from the pond. What is the most likely effect on this ecosystem over the next few weeks?

options.text: Only the pondweed is affected; the tadpoles and small fish remain unchanged
The tadpoles lose a food source and hiding place, so their numbers fall, and the small fish that eat tadpoles are then also affected
The small fish population increases because there is more open water
The tadpoles increase because there is no longer any competition for food

teacher.key_rationale: Removing pondweed affects connected populations, not just the plant itself: tadpoles lose food and shelter so their numbers drop, and this in turn affects the fish that feed on them. Option A is the trap for a student who believes a change affects only the component that directly changes; C and D contradict the loss of resources.
